units.text: Daniel’s Bayesian analysis of COVID origins

tl;dr I get 96% zoonosis (not 98% as in an early tweet). I'm not actually that confident - people disagree with me and I could be wrong. The calculation is also a bit weird in that the genetic evidence points away from zoonosis somewhat strongly but the epidemiological data points towards zoonosis even more strongly - I don't think you should expect this sort of split.
Note: all these numbers are sort of pulled out of my ass after watching the COVID origins debate. In particular, you should be aware that I haven’t actually read the primary literature here.
All ratios will put lab leak first, then zoonosis. So a prior of 8:15 means zoonosis is more likely.
Priors of zoonotic spillovers in Wuhan:

Zoonotic spillover pandemic happens maybe once every 20 years, let’s say a 2% chance it happens in Wuhan given population size. That gives you p(zoonotic spillover in Wuhan in 2020) = (1/20) * (1/50) = 1/1,000.
Prior of LL in Wuhan given DEFUSE, WIV, no known backbone at WIV:
P(WIV does sarbecovirus GoF research in 2020) = 1 / 4
P(they do it with a backbone of an unknown virus | they do it) = 1 / 6
P(it starts a pandemic | it leaks) = 1 / 2
So p(lab leak in Wuhan in 2020) = 1 / (4 * 6 * 100 * 2) = 1 / 5,000
First known outbreak is centred at HSM (Huanan Seafood Market), not elsewhere in Wuhan
Under zoonosis, there are like 4 markets it could be at, but maybe HSM is the biggest, so I’ll give that 1 / 3.

Under lab leak, I think it’s pretty unlikely to get to the HSM. Maybe not as unlikely as Peter says, but still pretty unlikely - I’ll give that 1 / 1,000. NB: this is by far my biggest disagreement with Rootclaim.
Gives a likelihood ratio of 3:1,000
First known outbreak is centred at HSM, not some random farm / truck driver of wildlife
Makes total sense under lab leak
Under zoonosis it’s a bit weird but I think mostly expected - I’ll give that 3 / 4 chance.
Also that one guy (Chen?) who got a case early
Pretty unreliable, you expect random shit, I’d give that as 1:1.
Environmental samples at market where wild animals are being sold.
Right where you expect them to be under zoonosis.

Under lab leak, they could have been in any of the stalls. Peter says there are 10 wild animal stalls out of 680 total - but only a subset of the stalls are tested. This is because they think it’s a zoonotic spillover, but they think that because of evidence we’ve already updated on, so we don’t want to double-count that. I think this reduces the factor to 1/30 or so.

But… IDK this still feels high. If it weren’t that exact pattern under zoonosis, you could explain it by saying some animals got other animals sick (e.g. with the drains as a vector). I think I want to mark it down by a factor of 2.
No animal vendors testing positive
I think this is a bit weird for zoonosis. Peter says it’s sort of similar to what happened with SARS, but I think this is like a 2 to 1 penalty.
Outbreak happens during winter
OK seasonality but maybe lab leaks are more likely to spread person-to-person during winter? I think I don’t want to count this as evidence.
Lineage A/B (key thing: no sequenced cases at market are lineage A, but some swabs get lineage A virus)
If lineage A didn’t start at market, why are earliest cases so close?
If lineage A was widespread, why isn’t it more diverse?
If lineage A wasn’t widespread, why was the market the only superspreading event?
So I think this is weird under the zoonosis story. First 12 cases are B, not A - which is weird under 2 spillovers. There’s some correlation, so I think I want to treat that as four 50% coincidences.
Likelihood ratio for no market-linked cases being B: 16:1
Low initial genetic diversity

I think there was some dispute about this that I don’t think really got resolved. My current take is that it isn’t a big deal - COVID can’t have been that pre-adapted to humans, given how impressive delta and omicron were. But I reserve my right to add a likelihood ratio here if there was something fishy.
FCS is hard to spread via fecal-oral in bats
FCS is great: you do expect messing around with cleavage sites under DEFUSE. But you also could see this in nature. I say:

FCS is hard to spread via fecal-oral in bats, so it had to develop in the intermediate host. (at least, everyone seems to agree on that, it’s a bit confusing to me). Intuitively this feels like 2:1 if I imagine the intermediate host is half the pre-human lifetime of the virus. But maybe it’s not? Let’s go with this:

12 nt insert is also kinda rare. Peter says it’s off-frame but I don’t quite buy that. But also, most published work talks about evolving FCSs rather than inserting them de novo - and you could get it from an animal host. I think this favours lab leak world, but not hugely.

CGG is a rare way to spell the arginine amino acid. I think in zoonosis world, we say that the first one is a 1 in 30 coincidence, and let’s say it was duplicated (which is a 1 / 2 coincidence). In lab leak world, it’s also weird, because we only use that codon maybe 1/10 of the time. If I take that seriously I’m going to give a 3x Bayes factor, but during the debate I thought it was more like 5-10x and Peter says it’s 5x, so let’s say it’s uh 7x
Alanine - got to be less than 1 in 5?
Initial P - not sure what the factor is but it’s low.

It’s markedly worse than all the FCS’s Peter showed labs actually insert for GoF. Laplace law of succession says that that’s a 1/7 probability under lab leak, and I think I’ll go with that? Conversely this seems like exactly the sort of thing that evolution does.
Likelihood ratio: 1:7 (so cancels out with CGG LR)
No “smoking gun” that it’s a lab leak (e.g. backbone that WIV had, proof that the lab did FCS insertion, etc.) after 4 years
No intermediate host found after 4 years

Let’s do other analyses. What if I didn’t think the centring at the HSM was evidence? Then I’d have a posterior ratio of 768:75 ~= 10:1. So it really matters whether you think that under lab leak it’s likely that the first outbreak would be at the HSM. I think it’s not, but I suppose I could be wrong.
Next analysis: what if I have a non-GoF lab leak theory? This would involve throwing out the genetic evidence which made the lab leak theory look better, but you get a better prior on lab leak:
P(WIV does sarbecovirus research 2020) = 1 / 1.5
P(they do it with an unknown virus | they do it) = 1 / 6
P(it starts a pandemic | it leaks) = 1 / 2
This gives you a prior odds ratio of 1:2, and a posterior ratio of 384:90,000 ~= 1:225. So looks worse than the GoF theory.
Background beliefs informing this analysis:
China wanted to cover up COVID origins whether it was zoonosis or not.
The DEFUSE proposal is not actually a very close match to SARS-CoV-2, and it describes the GoF research happening at UNC.
Given what we know about superspreading events, there’s nothing special about the Huanan Seafood Market if COVID didn’t start from a zoonotic spillover there.
You just don’t get a huge likelihood ratio from weird things about the SARS-CoV-2 virus that give it more pandemic potential, because we’re conditioning on the emergence of a pandemic.
